text.p: These are the leading stories in Zimbabwe's state-owned Herald newspaper on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Zimbabwean government is planning to recruit new medical staff, including expatriates, if the country's junior doctors and nurses, on strike for salary increments and better working conditions, do not report back to work on Wednesday.
- State-owned Air Zimbabwe's aircraft technicians, who went on a go-slow two weeks ago over salary grievances, resumed normal work on Tuesday to allow for negotiations with management to continue.

- Zimbabwe's largest building society, the Central Africa Building Society (CABS), has cut the mortgage interest rate for owner-occupied residential property to 19 percent from 19.75 percent for most properties and to 17.25 percent for high density suburban houses.
